newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta call money traded at 17.0/17.5 percent.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta call money traded at 17.0/17.5 percent.

text.p: Jakarta call money fell to 17.0/17.5 percent from an early high of 19.0/20.0 percent on Tuesday morning, dealers said.
They said an early central bank offer of SBIs repo seemed to have settled the market, pulling swap rates down across the board and helping to ease pressure in the interbank market.
One foreign bank dealer said he expected short-term rates to ease further on anticipation of further easing.
Overnight swaps eased to 1.0/1.1 from a high of 1.3 points and tom/next to 0.9/1.1 from 1.15/1.20 points.
Dealers said worry over tight liquidity was temporary and they expected the market to ease after the lunar new year and the Eid al-Fitr celebrations starting at the end of the week.
Bank Indonesia offered SBIs repo totalling 300 billion rupiah at 14.25 percent to stabilise high rupiah demand.
The bank kept its rates for bilateral SBIs stable on Tuesday. It offered eight-day SBIs at nine percent, two-week at 10.0 percent, one- and three-month at 11.25 and 12.00 percent.
The average overnight interbank rate on Monday was 18.06 percent, compared with 19.65 percent on Friday.
Bond dealers said the market remained quiet as they were reluctant to do anything shortly before the long weekend.
The stock market will be closed from February 7 to 11 and reopen on February 12. The foreign exchange and money market will be closed on February 10 and 11 and reopen on February 12.
One bond dealer said some offshore interest was seen in the $150 million five-year medium-term notes of PT Semen Gresik issued recently.
The yield of the benchmark PLN V/A bond was steady at 15.37 percent at the price of 105.25 percent.
